bull_bear.body: No capital-raise update was given on this call — notable, since at Q4FY26 the Board had approved raising **up to ₹2,000cr of equity, planned for H2FY27**. Neither the raise nor the RBI universal-banking-licence re-application (application returned by RBI on 13-Apr-2026) was mentioned by management or asked by any analyst. Capital is otherwise being deployed into 144 branches, ₹250cr of capacity building, and funding 25% asset growth; refinance/IBPC/securitisation lines are being deliberately preserved as unused funding optionality.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body:
- **The upgrade rests on a timing artefact plus a cycle.** ₹250cr of spend was deferred out of Q1 and must land in Q2-Q4; the implied path is *flat* quarterly profits from ₹317cr. If capacity spend slips again, FY27 beats but FY28 carries the cost.
- **Cost of funds has bottomed while deposit competition is live.** Rate hikes already taken in June; bulk-deposit ratio pinned at ~30%; management concedes "*marginal increase has been expected*" in funding cost. NIM defence now depends entirely on asset mix.
- **MSME yield is being deliberately given away** for ticket size (11-11.5% → ~10.5%). Management's defence is that opex and risk savings offset it — an argument that only proves out with seasoning, and the book is at 54% YoY growth.
- **Micro-mortgage PAR and GNPA are both drifting up** (1.2%→1.5%, 0.47%→0.55%) on a 3-year-old, ₹1,800cr book. Explained as natural maturation; the 18/24-MOB cohorts at <2.5% are the number to keep testing.
- **Gold new-to-bank mix jumped to ~40% in one quarter** — a genuine acquisition win, but a sharp shift in customer profile for a business the bank itself calls new.
- **Macro:** strengthening El Niño and kharif sowing delay explicitly flagged as a key monitorable for H2 economic activity; West Asia situation still fluid.
- **Silence on the capital raise and the universal-banking licence** — both were central to the Q4FY26 narrative and neither was addressed. Watch for reintroduction in Q2.
- **MD & CEO Sanjeev Nautiyal was absent (indisposed)** and the call was led by the ED. A one-off on the evidence available, but worth noting.
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Confident and unusually specific on operating capacity — Ashish Goel repeatedly answered "where will the mix settle?" questions by refusing to give ratios and giving *monthly disbursement capacity* instead (₹350-375cr AH, ₹100cr → ₹140-150cr MM, ₹230-250cr gold), which is a harder and more falsifiable commitment than a mix percentage. Kamath was candid that Q1's profit strength was a spending-deferral effect rather than run-rate, which is the opposite of guidance-padding. Product-level ROA and vertical-wise PPOP breakeven were both declined twice ("*we are not looking to give any product level numbers*"). The upgrade to ROA guidance one quarter after a conservative downgrade is a meaningful credibility event either way: last quarter's ~1.6% now looks like it was under-promising, exactly as several analysts alleged at the time.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body:
- **The credit-cost guidance basis quietly changed** from average gross loan book to average total assets. A 1.4-1.5%-of-GLB guide and a 0.9-1.0%-of-assets guide are much closer than the headline suggests — some of the apparent 50bps "cut" is denominator, not improvement. Management disclosed the change openly, but a like-for-like comparison requires the adjustment.
- **Last quarter's ROA guidance was challenged by four separate analysts as too conservative; one quarter later it was raised by 20-40bps.** The Walk-the-Talk read is that this management under-promises — useful calibration for how to treat the 25% asset growth and 56% secured-mix guides.
- **Being a late entrant into gold loans became a compliance advantage:** "*As RBI also came up with policies, we were already following most of the policies as this business is new to us*" — a rare case where absence of legacy practice is the moat.
- **Retail TD is now cheaper than bulk TD**, inverting the usual funding hierarchy and quietly changing the liability strategy toward retail momentum rather than bulk convenience.
- **MSME is explicitly being run as a low-ROA/high-ROE leveraged product** with non-fund-based and liability spin-offs as the real prize — an admission, agreed to directly by the CCO, that the segment's standalone economics are not the point.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- CRAR of 20.36% and Tier I CRAR of 19.16% as at Jun'26, down from 22.77% and 21.18% at Jun'25, on Total Capital of ₹6,923 Cr against Credit Risk Weighted Assets of ₹34,011 Cr.
- Net worth grew to ₹7,144 Cr at Jun'26 from ₹6,191 Cr at Jun'25 (Capital ₹1,945 Cr, Reserves and Surplus ₹5,100 Cr); BVPS shown at ₹35.1 for FY26.
- Floating provision of ~₹181 Cr "continues to be on books", of which ₹30 Cr is earmarked toward Tier II capital, ₹130 Cr for PCR calculation and ~₹21 Cr for other provisions; PCR at 85% and Total Provision ₹999 Cr.
- Liquidity is described as "Calibrated optimization while remaining well above regulatory threshold" with Avg. LCR for Q1FY27 around 132%.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

business.body:
- **Micro banking:** ₹21,371cr, +16.8% YoY. Bucket-X CE 99.68%; annualised slippages 1.72% (from 2.68% in Q4FY26); MFI PCR ~95%; slippages "less than 2%". All states stabilised; four-lender-and-above exposure now **below 1.5%** post-guardrails. Growth demand seen across states except Kerala, where the bank is deliberately not growing; branch additions skewed to UP, Rajasthan and Bihar.
- **Affordable housing + micro mortgages:** ₹11,210cr, +40.8% YoY. AH distributed via 581 branches (yield ~12.5%, ticket ₹16-20 lakh, urban/semi-urban, minimal metro presence, GNPA 1.2%); micro mortgages ~₹1,800cr via 323 branches (yield ~19.5%, ~70% semi-urban, average ticket ₹7-8 lakh, GNPA 0.6%). MM PAR rose 1.2% → ~1.5% and NPA 0.47% → 0.55% — attributed to a 3-year-old book's natural seasoning, with 18/24-MOB cohorts still below 2.5%.
- **MSME:** ₹3,470cr, **+54% YoY**. Working capital + supply-chain finance ≈ 28% of the MSME book. PAR down 13bps; new-book GNPA 0.5%. Deliberate move up the ticket-size curve (LAP ₹58-60L → ₹80-90L; WC ₹70-80L → ₹1.1-1.2cr) trading yield (11-11.5% → ~10.5%) for lower opex and access to non-fund-based/liability relationships.
- **Gold loans:** ₹1,020cr, **+248.6% YoY**; disbursements ₹467cr, +183.9% YoY; sourced from 455 branches (+106 in the quarter). Origination LTV 75%, book LTV 56%. New-to-bank mix jumped to ~40% on branch activation plus rising MFI-customer demand. Loan-officer productivity reaches ₹25-30 lakh within a year of a branch going live.
- **Vehicle finance:** ₹1,036cr, +85.1% YoY, GNPA 1.7%, across 337 branches; mix being pushed toward mid-premium and EV 2-wheelers.
- **New business lines combined (gold + vehicle + agri):** **7% of gross loan book, 9% of Q1 disbursements** (vs ~6% of mix at Q4FY26).
- **Liabilities:** Ivory HNI programme scaling; insurance cross-sell penetration up; mutual-fund distribution now on mobile/net banking; co-branded credit card in testing; FCNR-B capacity being used (₹60cr raised in Q1). Liability focus stays on top-8/top-30 markets, where CASA is growing ~75% YoY and overall deposits ~36%.

business.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers (listed names)

business.body:
- Journey slide traces Ujjivan Financial Services Ltd. (UFSL) registered as an NBFC with RBI in 2004-05, UFSL IPO listed May 2016, Ujjivan SFB IPO listed Dec 2019, and states the bank "Navigated major crises and built India's leading SFB. Completed reverse merger with Holding Company in 2024".
- Pan-India franchise described as 26 States and UTs, 347 Districts and 814 Branches (206 URCs), with a partnership-led Electronic Collection Retail Points network so Micro Banking customers can pay EMIs without coming to centre meetings or branches.
- Liability franchise framed as retail-led: Total Deposits ₹48,129 Cr grew 24.6% YoY (described as "Highest yearly growth in last 10 quarters") and Retail TD+CASA at ₹32,716 Cr, up 17% YoY.
- Deck presents scale as "1 Cr+ Customer Franchise" with 5 Lakh+ loans processed/month and 10.5 Cr+ transactions generating/month; deposit customers rose from 62.1 lakh (FY22) to 97.4 lakh (FY26).
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Reverse merger] Deck records completion of the reverse merger with the Holding Company in 2024, following UFSL's 2016 listing and Ujjivan SFB's Dec 2019 listing.
- [Regulation] Underwriting operates within "MFIN Guardrails" — disbursements allowed up to 60 DPD with other lenders at the time of disbursement — while Ujjivan's own policy "Precludes customer with 1 DPD with Ujjivan at the time of disbursement".
- [Credit guarantee] Book covered under CGFMU as on Jun'26 is ₹1,228 Cr; NNPA as of Jun'26 at 0.34%.
- [Lender overlap] Share of GL book "Unique to Ujjivan" rose from 49.7% (Jun'25) to 57.1% (Jun'26), and for IL from 56.7% to 67.8%, with Ujjivan+3 and above shrinking.
- [Shareholding] Shareholding pattern as on Jun'26 is presented as Foreign Institutional Investors (FPI, FPC & FDI) 16.8%, Domestic Institutional Investors (MF, AIF, Ins & QIB) 33.5% and Retail & Others 49.7%, with Sundaram MF, IFC and Axis MF heading the top-10 investor list.
business.title: Notable from the deck

latest_quarter.body:
- NIM **stable at 8.5%** despite cost of funds falling to 6.86% — the yield mix is doing the work: MFI recovery holding blended yields up, plus gold/2-wheeler/used-car/micro-mortgage as the high-yield offsets against affordable housing (~12.5%) and the deliberately de-yielded MSME book (~10.5%).
- **Cost-of-funds tailwind is over.** CRO Brajesh Cherian: "*From the repricing side… we can't see further visibility on repricing benefit. We feel it would remain at the current level or slightly elevated.*" Deposit rates were raised in June; no further hikes seen as immediately necessary. IBPC, refinance and securitisation are held in reserve as margin-stabilising levers (unused in Q1).
- Retail TD is now **cheaper than bulk TD** — a reversal management flagged, and the reason retail-TD momentum is being pushed.
- Opex: personnel cost up on April increments/hiring/gratuity-leave; other expenses down sequentially on lower business-generation and CSR spend. Full-year opex-to-ATA guided **down** to 6.4% (better than earlier plan) purely because ₹250cr of capacity spend slipped out of Q1 and efficiencies landed.
- Credit cost 0.9% in Q1 vs 2.2% in FY26 — the single biggest ROA swing factor and the trigger for the guidance upgrade.
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

latest_quarter.body:
- **Q1 FY27 (this):** GLB ₹42,903cr (+28.9% YoY), deposits ₹48,129cr (+25%), CASA ₹12,930cr (+37.8%); secured crossed half the book at 50.4% (+42.7% YoY); PAT ₹317cr, ROA 2.2%, ROE 18.2%; NIM stable 8.5%, cost of funds 6.86%; GNPA 2.17% (-10bps), PCR 85%, credit cost 0.9%; MFI annualised slippages 1.72% (from 2.68%), borrower base grew for the first time in 8 quarters (1.72 lakh adds). **Guidance upgraded**: FY27 ROA 1.8-2.0% (was ~1.6%), credit cost 0.9-1.0% of avg assets (basis changed from avg GLB), opex 6.4% of avg assets (better than plan). Reaffirmed: 25% asset growth, 56% secured by exit-March-27, 144 branches (38 done), ₹250cr capacity spend. Gold ₹1,020cr (+249%), vehicle ₹1,036cr (+85%), MSME ₹3,470cr (+54%). MD absent; ED Carol Furtado led. **No mention of the ₹2,000cr capital raise or the RBI universal-banking re-application.**
- _Q2 FY27 → check: whether the ₹250cr capacity spend actually lands (quarterly profit should stay ~flat vs ₹317cr if it does); opex-to-ATA tracking to 6.4%; credit cost holding 0.9-1.0%; 106 remaining branches opening on schedule; secured mix progressing 50.4% → 56%; gold active branches toward 575 and monthly disbursements toward ₹230-250cr; micro-mortgage PAR/GNPA drift; cost of funds after the June rate hikes; re-emergence of the ₹2,000cr capital raise and universal-banking licence plan._
latest_quarter.title: QoQ change log (fill each quarter)

outlook.body:
- **ROA: raised to 1.8-2.0% for FY27** (from ~1.6% guided at Q4FY26) — driven, in management's ordering, "*on Opex first and credit cost next*"; deposit-pricing pressure is stated to be already baked in.
- **Credit cost: revised down to 0.9-1.0% of average total assets** for FY27 (basis deliberately changed from average GLB to average balance sheet "for better alignment").
- **Opex: ~6.4% of average assets for FY27** — *lower* than earlier planned, because of deferred spend plus efficiency gains; guided to improve year-on-year beyond FY27 as investments taper.
- **Asset growth: 25% for FY27**, reaffirmed ("*reinforced our confidence in achieving our FY '27 planned asset growth of 25%*").
- **Loan mix: 56% secured by exit-March 2027** — unchanged from the Q4FY26 guide, explicitly reaffirmed ("*we maintain the same guidance of 56%*").
- **Capacity-building spend: ~₹250cr through FY27** (branch opening, branding, tech & analytics) — started only in June, to build up across remaining quarters.
- **Branches: 144 new branches in FY27**; 38 opened in Q1, **106 still to open**.
- **Gold loans:** active gold-loan branches to go from ~430-440 to **~575 by end-FY27** (gold to be activated in ~250 branches during the year); monthly disbursement to exit March at **~₹230-250cr/month** (from ~₹160-175cr/month currently). Long-term intent: gold loan offered from *almost all* branches.
- **Micro mortgages:** monthly disbursement capacity from ~₹100cr/month now to **₹140-150cr/month exit-March**; affordable-housing capacity already built at ₹350-375cr/month. Incremental disbursement mix to tilt toward micro mortgages.
- **CASA:** current CASA growth rate to be maintained; CASA ratio target (~30%) "*we are very much committed or we may over deliver slightly.*"
- **Bulk deposits:** to be held **at/around 30%** of deposits.
- **Cost of funds:** repricing benefit exhausted — expected to stay at current level "*or slightly elevated*"; **no immediate need for further deposit rate hikes** after the June increases.
- **MFI credit cost:** guided unsecured credit cost of 2% to come in "*just a little lower than that*" (Q1 ran at 1.9% of MFI GLP).
- **Pre-owned cars:** piloted in Karnataka; to be **tested in 2-3 geographies this year and scaled next year**. **HCV/LCV entry only after FY27** ("*if and when we plan would be only after this financial year*").
- **MSME ticket-size band:** LAP moved to ₹80-90 lakh and working capital to ₹1.1-1.2cr; management will hold this band for the rest of FY27 and revisit "probably next year."
outlook.title: Guidance (CRITICAL — verify next quarter)

outlook.body: Not applicable (bank). Pipeline proxies: disbursements ₹9,245cr (+41.4% YoY); **1.72 lakh new micro-banking customers added in Q1 — borrower base growing for the first time after seven quarters of degrowth**; 106 branches still to open this year; gold-loan and micro-mortgage monthly disbursement capacities being built toward stated March-exit run-rates. New product pipeline: Unsecured Fast Track (digital, account-aggregator + bureau based) pilot complete and ready to scale; pre-owned cars piloted; mid-corporate lending disbursed its first loans in Q1; MSME suite extended with purchase-invoice discounting; co-branded credit card in testing.
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body: Gold (₹1,020cr → targeting ₹230-250cr/month disbursement exit-run-rate), micro mortgages (the yield-defence engine at ~19.5%), MSME working capital/supply-chain finance, and four genuinely new engines started this quarter: **Unsecured Fast Track** (fully digital, account-aggregator-based, pilot complete and ready to scale), **pre-owned cars** (Karnataka pilot done), **mid-corporate lending** (first disbursements in Q1) and **purchase-invoice discounting**. Management explicitly framed gold as a late-entrant advantage — being new meant they were already compliant when RBI's gold-loan rules landed — and sees the under-penetrated East/Northeast/North as their opening against a South-heavy incumbent market.

deepdive.thesis: The clearest guidance *upgrade* in the SFB space this quarter: three months after guiding FY27 ROA down to ~1.6%, Ujjivan raised it to **1.8-2.0%**, cut FY27 credit-cost guidance to **0.9-1.0% of average assets** and lowered planned opex to **6.4% of average assets** — on the back of MFI annualised slippages halving (2.68% → 1.72%), Bucket-X collection efficiency holding at 99.68% and a borrower base that grew for the first time after seven quarters of contraction. Q1 delivered ROA 2.2% / ROE 18.2% with the secured book crossing the halfway mark (50.4%) at 42.7% YoY growth, so the FY27 question shifts from "can they earn" to whether the deferred ₹250cr capacity-building spend and deposit-side pricing pressure claw back the beat over H2.
